The slow return of the River Alder salmon

For forty years the River Alder ran silent in autumn. This year the first fish were counted at the Tollgate weir on the ninth of October.

A river rebuilt

Taking the weirs out

Three weirs came down between 2019 and 2023. Each was a small concrete step, no taller than a kitchen table, but together they cut the river into four disconnected pools.

Replanting the banks

Alder, willow and hazel were planted along nine kilometres of bank. The shade keeps summer water below fifteen degrees, which matters more to young salmon than any fish ladder.

We did not bring the salmon back. We stopped stopping them.

What the counts show

  1. 2023: no adult salmon recorded.
  2. 2024: four adults recorded at Tollgate.
  3. 2025: thirty-one adults recorded, six reaching the upper pools.

Caveats

Counts depend on autumn rain; a dry October hides fish that are already in the river.
